draft.title: Indigenous peoples under international law
card: The United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP) was adopted by the UN General Assembly in 2007. It sets out the rights of Indigenous peoples around the world.
Its rights include the right to practise and keep their culture, the right to their lands, territories and resources, and the right to self-determination.
A declaration is a statement of agreed standards. It is not a treaty, so it does not bind states in the way a treaty does. Its force comes from the commitment states make to it.
Australia did not support the Declaration in 2007. It endorsed it in 2009, which means it formally gave its support.
draft.remember: UNDRIP (2007) sets standards on culture, land and self-determination. Australia endorsed it in 2009.

a.q: Which of these is a right set out in the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples?
opts: The right of Indigenous peoples to their lands and culture
The right of states to override Indigenous laws
The right of Indigenous peoples to veto all national laws
The right of Indigenous peoples to leave their home state
a.why: The Declaration sets out rights to culture, land and self-determination. The other options describe powers it does not give, such as overriding national law or a general veto.
a.clue: Think of the three areas of rights the Declaration covers.

b.q: A student says Australia is legally bound by the Declaration in the same way as by a treaty it has ratified. Which reply is most accurate?
opts: The Declaration is a statement of standards, not a treaty
The Declaration is a treaty, but Australia only endorsed it
The Declaration became binding when Australia endorsed it
The Declaration binds only states that voted against it
b.why: A declaration states agreed standards and is not a treaty, so it does not bind states in the way a treaty does. Endorsing it shows support but does not turn it into a treaty, which is why the third option is tempting but wrong.
b.clue: Ask what kind of document a declaration is.

a.best: The right of Indigenous peoples to their lands and culture

b.best: The Declaration is a statement of standards, not a treaty

a.q: Which of these is a right set out in the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples?
opts: The right of Indigenous peoples to their lands and culture
The right of states to override Indigenous laws
The right of Indigenous peoples to veto all national laws
